speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked	the Minister for Law (a) whether the Government will review the current annual disposable income criteria for a person to qualify for legal aid; (b) what are the reasons for applicants failing to qualify for legal aid; and (c) among applicants who qualify for legal aid, what are the broad categories of their cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Ministry of Law regularly reviews the means test to ensure that those who are unable to afford to hire a lawyer can still obtain legal advice or representation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: We will continue to monitor and review the criteria for the means test regularly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The applicants who were granted legal aid were helped in a wide range of civil matters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: A more complete list of services offered by the Legal Aid Bureau can be found on its website.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: What are the avenues for appeal, and can they appeal to Legal Aid for help and whether	 there are any other avenues that they can go to?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: However, if it is a means issue and you do not fall within the legal aid means test, there are other possibilities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the Pro Bono Services Office is one option.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is located in the State Courts itself.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a charitable organisation but it is working on this joint project with the State Courts where lawyers contribute their time and service on a discounted basis.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You can go to the first floor of the State Courts, take a left turn, the office is there.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They will direct you to the place to go accordingly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, these are for people who fall through the gap, if you like, where they cannot easily afford their own lawyer but, at the same time, do not meet the means test for legal aid.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the reason for rejection happens to be that they do not meet the merits test, then that would be really quite difficult because, obviously, they do not have a good case.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It would not be useful to pursue the claim when there is no merit.
